Exact install command and method (pip, standalone installer, uv self update, winget, or other)
Full error output or the message Trellix shows when it blocks the file, and whether the block happens on download or on execution
Whether the blocked file matches the published uv.exe hash for the failing release
external_evidence: Reporter says Trellix Endpoint Security blocks the uv*.exe files during install with no reason given, and that older versions install fine. Playbook rules 5 and 8 treat antivirus blocking of a release binary as an external cause. Related closed issues #17344 (Defender reports 0.9.22 installer as containing a virus or unwanted software) and #1587 (Defender false positive on the release zip) show the same pattern.

related_issues.reason: Same pattern: a Windows antivirus flags a fresh uv release binary during install. Different product (Defender, not Trellix) and closed as completed, so context only.
Windows Defender quarantining uv binaries on a fresh install. Closed as duplicate; a related antivirus symptom, not the same report.
Old Defender false-positive report on a uv release zip. Similar symptom in a different AV product and era.
Windows install failure with access denied during a cache rename. Different error and cause, only a loosely similar Windows install symptom.

escalation_reason: A security product is flagging uv release binaries, so a maintainer should check whether the flagged file matches the published release. Playbook rule 8 calls for escalation on antivirus flags.
rationale: The reporter's own text says Trellix blocks the uv*.exe install files with no reason shown, and that older versions work, so uv itself is not shown to fail. This matches the playbook's antivirus-flag rule, so the likely cause is external, with the fix belonging to the AV vendor or to a false-positive report. Type is bug because the reporter describes a release-triggered install failure, but the confidence is medium because the cause could also be a real change in 11.9 that the AV reacts to. Search for Trellix found no prior issues, and two Defender false-positive issues were closed as external or duplicate. No canonical tracking issue was found. The version numbers in the report do not match uv's scheme, so the exact breaking release could not be confirmed.
